secoes.corpo:
A obstetric nursing occupies a privileged position in the maternal-child care line: it is the link between prenatal care, childbirth, and initial newborn care. The obstetric scales are instruments that systematize clinical assessment in these three critical moments, supporting decisions that directly impact maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.

O Bishop Score , described by Edward Bishop in 1964, is the quintessential obstetric scale. It assesses five characteristics of the cervix — dilation, effacement, consistency, position, and fetal station — to predict the likelihood of successful labor induction. A favorable Bishop score (> 8 points) is associated with a vaginal delivery rate of 80-90%, while an unfavorable Bishop score ( At the moment of birth, the transition to immediate neonatal care is mediated by the Apgar score . Although classified as a neonatal scale, its application at the 1st and 5th minute of life is inseparable from obstetric care — the obstetric nurse is responsible for the initial assessment of the newborn and must communicate the Apgar score to the team as an indicator of fetal-neonatal transition. The scales of Ballard e Capurro complete the picture by allowing the estimation of postnatal gestational age, essential information for classifying the newborn (preterm, term, or post-term) and for defining clinical management.

Introduction to Obstetric Scales
A obstetric nursing occupies a privileged position in the maternal-child care line: it is the link between prenatal care, childbirth, and initial newborn care. The obstetric scales are instruments that systematize clinical assessment in these three critical moments, supporting decisions that directly impact maternal and neonatal morbidity and mortality.

O Bishop Score , described by Edward Bishop in 1964, is the quintessential obstetric scale. It assesses five characteristics of the cervix — dilation, effacement, consistency, position, and fetal station — to predict the likelihood of successful labor induction. A favorable Bishop score (> 8 points) is associated with a vaginal delivery rate of 80-90%, while an unfavorable Bishop score ( At the moment of birth, the transition to immediate neonatal care is mediated by the Apgar score . Although classified as a neonatal scale, its application at the 1st and 5th minute of life is inseparable from obstetric care — the obstetric nurse is responsible for the initial assessment of the newborn and must communicate the Apgar score to the team as an indicator of fetal-neonatal transition. The scales of Ballard e Capurro complete the picture by allowing the estimation of postnatal gestational age, essential information for classifying the newborn (preterm, term, or post-term) and for defining clinical management.

Scales and Calculators

Bishop
Bishop Score

Assesses cervical conditions for labor induction. 5 parameters: dilation, effacement, consistency, position, and station. Score 0-13.

Apgar
Newborn Vitality

Universal assessment of neonatal vitality at 1st and 5th minute. Color, HR, reflexes, tone, and respiration. Communication with the obstetric team.

Ballard
New Ballard Score

Accurate estimation of gestational age. 12 parameters. Gold standard for classifying preterm and term newborns.

Capurro
Gestational Age

Rapid method for postnatal gestational age. 5 somatic parameters. Suitable for newborns above 29 weeks.

CRIES
Neonatal Postoperative Pain

Pain assessment in newborns. Complements integrated mother-baby care in the postoperative period.
